strengths_deep_dive: The Islamic Scholarship Fund stands out for its exceptional alumni outcomes and focused strategic niche. Rather than providing generic direct aid, ISF focuses on capacity building within public policy, media, and law. This strategy has yielded concrete results, including <cite id="5">746 prestigious awards granted</cite> and over <cite id="5">$3.67 million invested into student awards</cite>. Outcome metrics demonstrate that <cite id="5">88% of program alumni successfully secure employment</cite> in their direct field of study, while maintaining a <cite id="4">100% graduation rate</cite>. Additionally, governance practices are strong; the organization holds a Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid and maintains <cite id="1">100% independent board members</cite>.
rich_narrative.summary: Founded in 2009, the Islamic Scholarship Fund (ISF) is a national organization dedicated to increasing American Muslim representation in media, journalism, public policy, and law <cite id="4">through targeted grants and fellowships</cite>. By addressing the historical underrepresentation of American Muslims in public-facing and policy-shaping fields, ISF seeks to cultivate future leaders and storytellers. In FY2024, the organization posted substantial revenue growth, generating <cite id="3">$1,922,887 in total revenue</cite>, supported by a strong three-year revenue CAGR of 36.5%. ISF operates as a <cite id="2">zakat-eligible institution</cite>, routing funds to eligible students and fellows under the fi sabilillah category. The organization maintains a <cite id="1">91.7 out of 100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite> and has achieved a <cite id="1">100% score in Leadership and Culture</cite>. With an operational program expense ratio of 65.0% in FY2024 (and a cash-adjusted program ratio score of 65%), ISF delivers high-touch fellowship and scholarship programs, investing over <cite id="5">$3.67 million cumulatively in awards</cite> since its inception.
